commit_message:
Add an experimental fix to avoid attempting to mmap memory from an offset that is not a multiple of the system page size on systems with page sizes larger than 32KB.

fix_commit.message: Fix the VFSes so that there is no 32-bit integer overflow in the xShmMap method if the WAL file size exceeds about 25 terabytes, or if the header is corrupted to make SQLite think that the WAL file size is that big. [bugs:/info/2026-05-21T03:53:03Z|Bug 2026-05-21T03:53:03Z].
fix_commit.author: drh

findings.title: 32-bit integer overflow in unixShmMap() byte-count computation
findings.message: In unixShmMap() (src/os_unix.c), the variable `nByte` is declared as `int` but computed as `nReqRegion * szRegion`, where both operands are 32-bit integers. When the WAL file is very large (>~25TB) or a corrupted WAL header causes SQLite to believe the file is that large, `nReqRegion` can be enormous and the multiplication silently wraps to a small or negative value. The overflowed `nByte` is then used in a file-size comparison (`sStat.st_size < nByte`) that may incorrectly pass, and subsequently as the length argument to file-write and mmap calls—causing an under-sized mapping. Downstream reads and writes through the mapped region then access memory outside the intended bounds. Similarly, `nMap = szRegion * nShmPerMap` is also declared `int` and suffers the same overflow when `nShmPerMap` is large (e.g., on systems with 64KB OS pages).
findings.suggestion: Widen all byte-count variables that are products of region counts and region sizes to i64 (sqlite3_int64) before the multiplication, and cast at least one operand to i64 so the multiplication is performed in 64-bit arithmetic. For example: `i64 nByte = nReqRegion*(i64)szRegion;` and `i64 nMap = (i64)szRegion*(i64)nShmPerMap;`. Also widen loop/index variables (iPg, i) that are indexed over these 64-bit counts.

ground_truth.root_cause: The variables `nByte` and `nMap` were declared as `int` (32-bit) while the values they store are the product of a region count and a region size. For WAL indexes with very large (or corrupted) region counts, the product exceeds INT_MAX, causing signed integer overflow and yielding a small or negative byte count. This regression was introduced in commit 781e34cde3 (2014-03-20) when `nByte` was changed from `(iRegion+1)*szRegion` to the potentially much larger `nReqRegion*szRegion` to accommodate multi-region-per-map systems.
